title: Functorial resolutions on the entire bounded-above category
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $\mathcal F$ be a class of its objects containing zero and closed under isomorphisms, finite biproducts and direct summands (if $U\oplus V\in\mathcal F$, then $U,V\in\mathcal F$). Suppose there is a functor $P:A\to A$ with $P(M)\in\mathcal F$ for every $M$ and a natural transformation $\epsilon:P\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ with epimorphic components. Let $\mathrm{CoCh}^{-}(A)$ be the full subcategory of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees; an upper bound is not part of the data of an object. There is a functor $S:\mathrm{CoCh}^{-}(A)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(A)$ and a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota$, where $\iota$ is the inclusion, such that every $a_L:S(L)\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $S(L)$ belongs to $\mathcal F$, and for every integer $b$, $L^i=0$ for $i>b$ implies $S(L)^i=0$ for $i>b$. The functor acts on all maps of bounded-above complexes, including maps between complexes with different upper bounds.
